concerns.text: T012d-Execute depends on T008a (candidate generation) but T008a is marked 'FAILED: unspecified'. A consumer task (scraping) cannot proceed before its producer (source list generation) is successfully completed. This creates a blocking dependency violation.

T012a (Fetch Data) depends on T009c (sources.yaml). T009c depends on T008b (Verify Sources), which depends on T008a. Since T008a is marked 'FAILED', the entire chain T008a -> T008b -> T009c -> T012a is broken. The task order implies a valid flow, but the status of the producer (T008a) invalidates the consumer's ability to run.

T035 (Generate Paper Draft) depends on T031c (Generate Report YAML). T031c is listed as unimplemented/rejected in the analysis report. A consumer task (Paper Draft) cannot be scheduled before its producer (Report YAML) is defined and executable. This violates the producer-before-consumer rule.

T035 depends on T056 (Standardize Associational Framing), which is a revision task. Revision tasks are typically dependent on the completion of the base tasks they modify. The current ordering places T035 (final output) as dependent on a revision task that itself depends on T035 (via T031c -> T035 dependency loop implied by 'Update paper_draft.md'). This creates a circular dependency or a missing prerequisite for the final artifact.

T012d-Protocol is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but depends on T009c (sources.yaml). While the protocol definition itself might be independent of execution, the task description implies it uses 'verified/provisional sources'. If T009c is not complete, the protocol cannot be fully defined. The [P] tag may be misleading if the input artifact (sources.yaml) is not guaranteed to exist in parallel with other Phase 3 tasks.
